items.title: [AINews] LLMs can read & write neural network weights: "Weight Space Programming" cuts Autoresearch out of the RSI loop
items.description: Editing Qwen’s weights to reduce reasoning loops, DeepSeek’s super-agent prototype, and the GDPx benchmark.
items.summary: Researchers have developed a method called "Weight Space Programming," allowing large language models (LLMs) to directly edit neural network weights, potentially eliminating the need for human intervention in refining AI agents. This breakthrough could significantly impact autoresearch by reducing reasoning loops and improving efficiency in training advanced AI systems like DeepSeek’s super-agent prototype.
items.summary_detailed: Researchers have developed a method called "Weight Space Programming," allowing large language models (LLMs) like Qwen to directly edit neural network weights to reduce reasoning loops. This breakthrough enables DeepSeek's super-agent prototype to perform tasks more efficiently without human intervention in the reinforcement learning process. The technique has significant implications for automating complex problem-solving and could potentially streamline various industries relying on AI, including autonomous research systems (RSI), by reducing dependency on manual oversight.

• Editing Qwen's weights reduces reasoning loops.
